smells.finding: advance() is now ~110 lines and its why-capture region carries three mutually exclusive recording branches (if require_why / elif not why_exempt / else). The new branch is only ~10 lines, but it pushed a function that was already long past the point where the recording policy is readable in one pass. Extracting the decision -- e.g. a small _why_record_decision(t, why, mechanical, require_why) returning (append?, mechanical?, refusal_or_None) -- would let advance() read as: prove postconditions, decide the record, apply it. NON-BLOCKING: the branch is correct, exhaustively tested (M4/M5), and pre-existing length is not this gate's debt to pay.

The engine module is module-level functions, no classes. The new test class TripHardGuardsBeginNotClose carries 21 methods, but it has exactly one responsibility (the #467 band-semantics change), matching the file's established one-class-per-behaviour-cluster convention (TripTwoBandGatePolicy, RefreshRequestIdentity, TripRealGaugeFileWiring). A cohesive fixture is not a large class in Fowler's sense.

Mild and local, inside advance(): _append_why(cl, iid, why=why.strip(), mechanical=False) now appears twice (require_why branch and the non-exempt branch), and the guard expression (why or "").strip() appears three times in the same function. The two call sites can drift -- if a future change adds a field to the why record, one site can be updated and the other missed, and the failure mode is a silently absent understanding, which is precisely #431. NON-BLOCKING, but it is the same class of drift the gate's own _trip_hard_band_reading consolidation was introduced to prevent, applied one level down.

This change REDUCED it. Pre-change, _trip_hard_gate reached into _gauge_reader.thresholds_for(reading.model) and compared reading.fill_fraction itself. Post-change that knowledge lives in _trip_hard_band_reading and _trip_hard_gate asks only 'is the band active'. The guard no longer envies the reader.
The triple (cl, iid, base_dir) travels together through _trip_hard_gate, _trip_hard_band_reading, start, reopen, advance and dispatch -- a textbook clump that a ctx object would absorb.

Adding one defaulted keyword was the minimum that carries the band decision across the CLI boundary while leaving every direct caller byte-identical -- which I verified: no verb return string changed, and the whole 1815-test suite is green. The implementer also documented and defended the alternative it rejected (a second pre-verb guard in dispatch) in Assumption 1, on the sound ground that only advance can append to the why_trail, so a dispatch-level refusal would demand a --why that advance then discards on an exempt gate. The standard subordinates the smell because the shorter signature was not reachable without authority this gate did not hold.

smells.finding: REAL, and it drew blood. The single fact 'HARD blocks advance' was mirrored in four hand-maintained places: the engine's Trip module-header comment (:1217ff), docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's Trip section, that file's start/advance/reopen verb-table rows, and docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md:13. Changing one behaviour required editing all four; three were updated and the fourth was missed. I confirmed the miss with my own blast-radius grep -- GLOSSARY.md:13 still reads 'HARD blocks `advance` until the agent requests a context refresh', which is now false and is the glossary every constellation agent reads. The implementer found it too, correctly declined to edit it (out of allowed scope), and escalated. NON-BLOCKING for this gate because the escalation was the right move and the file was outside scope, but the smell is the root cause of triage candidate tc1 and it will recur on the next Trip change unless the mirrored prose gets a single source or a freshness check.

Worth noting the change actively resisted the smell where it could: the band decision was consolidated into one predicate rather than duplicated at the two call sites.

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md, Implementation discipline: 'Match the surrounding code's ... in-file documentation conventions.' The engine's established convention is dense why-comments citing the issue that produced the rule (#179, #182, #190, #191 all appear this way in surrounding code). Reinforced by CREW_CONTEXT.md's Verification Discipline, which treats the reason a guard exists as load-bearing knowledge.
override.reason: These comments record DECISION RATIONALE, not a paraphrase of the code: why advance is deliberately absent from the guarded set, what breaks without the no-silent-close rule (the _latest_why_record skip that yields a pre-trip DIGEST), and why the <why-id> placeholder was a silent no-op across four runs. That is exactly the knowledge that was lost between #182 and #431 and cost this issue. Fowler's smell is a comment standing in for unclear code; these stand in for a design record that has no other home in a single-file engine. Logged rather than flagged, with the extract-a-name option recorded above so it is not lost.
